nodes.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 1$ there are $i < n$ and a prime $p > n$ such that $p$ divides $n + 1 + i$. Thus one of the $n$ consecutive integers $n + 1, \dots, 2n$ has a prime divisor greater than $n$.
nodes.title: Bertrand's postulate in block form

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $s = n + 2$. If $s$ divides neither $k - 1$ nor $k - 2$ (natural-number differences, truncated at $0$), then $s$ divides $k + i$ for some $i < n$.

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers and put $N = k + n - 1$. If $n! \cdot N^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides $\binom{N}{n}$.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Schur criterion from the half-exponent bound

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. If some prime $p > n$ divides $k + i$ for some $i < n$, then some prime $q > n$ divides $\binom{k + n - 1}{n}$.
nodes.title: Large prime divisors pass from a block to its binomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $2 \le n < k$ be natural numbers with $n! \cdot 2^{n-1} < k$. Then some prime $p > n$ divides $\binom{k + n - 1}{n}$.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Schur criterion for blocks with a large start

nodes.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers, put $N = k + n - 1$, and let $\pi(n)$ be the number of primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot N^{\pi(n)} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides $\binom{N}{n}$.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Schur criterion from the prime-counting bound

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, let $\pi(n)$ be the number of primes at most $n$, and let $\lfloor\sqrt{k+n-1}\rfloor$ be the integer square root. If $2^{\pi(n)} \lfloor\sqrt{k+n-1}\rfloor < n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides $\binom{k+n-1}{n}$.
nodes.title: Large prime divisor of the block binomial coefficient from the smooth-number count

nodes.summary: Large prime divisor of the block binomial coefficient from the square-root primorial bound. Let $n \ge 1$ and $k > n$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$, let $\lfloor\sqrt{N}\rfloor$ be the integer square root of $N$ and let $P$ be the product of all primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot N^{\lfloor\sqrt{N}\rfloor + 1} \cdot P < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides $\binom{N}{n}$.
nodes.title: Large prime divisor of the block binomial coefficient from the square-root primorial bound

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $p$ be a prime with $p > n$ and $k \le p \le k + n - 1$. Then $p$ divides $\binom{k+n-1}{n}$.
nodes.title: Primes above $n$ in the block divide the block binomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j < n$, and let $r$ be a prime with $r > n$. If $r$ divides $k + j$, then $r$ divides $\binom{k+n-1}{n}$.
nodes.title: Prime divisors above $n$ of a block term divide the binomial coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 38$ and $k$ be natural numbers. If none of the $n$ consecutive integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$ has a prime divisor greater than $n$, then $k \le n^2$.
nodes.title: Blocks without large prime divisors start at most at $n^2$
